title: Separating two closed supports of a coherent module on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated; the last two conditions mean that every open cover has a finite subcover and the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Modules are on the small etale ringed site, with quasi-coherence as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ for the locus of nonzero geometric stalks, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A closed immersion is representable and a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduced means that etale scheme charts have local rings without nonzero nilpotents, and irreducible means nonempty and not the union of two proper closed subsets. Assume $X$ is Noetherian. Let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $T_1,T_2\subseteq|X|$ be closed subsets such that $\operatorname{Supp}(F)=T_1\cup T_2$. There is a coherent submodule $A\subseteq F$ for which $B=F/A$ is coherent and $$0\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow0$$ is exact, with $\operatorname{Supp}(A)\subseteq T_1$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(B)\subseteq T_2$. Quotients are cokernels in module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 07UP, lemma-prepare-filter-support, with Zprime = T_1 and Z = T_2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] to $T_2$, obtaining a reduced closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $|Z|=T_2$. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], its defining ideal $I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ is quasi-coherent, and its restriction under an etale base change is the defining ideal of the base-changed closed subspace. Define $A_n=I^nF$, with $I^0F=F$, by the locally generated products in [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-ideal-power], and set $B_n=F/A_n$. That same node states that both $A_n$ and $B_n$ are coherent for every $n\geq0$.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the open subspace with $|U|=|X|\setminus T_1$, using the open-subspace correspondence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. It is Noetherian: [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-topology] makes $|X|$ Noetherian, hence $U$ is quasi-compact. Explicitly, for any cover of $U$ by opens of $X$, choose a minimal complement in $X$ of a finite subunion. Adding any member cannot shrink this complement, so the finite subunion already covers $U$. The locally Noetherian condition is inherited because every etale scheme chart of $U$ is an etale scheme chart of $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Quasi-separatedness of a quasi-compact open subspace is supplied by [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Thus all three Noetherian conditions hold on $U$.

source.place: Tag 07UP, sentence that the open complement is Noetherian; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03BZ and 04ZF

proof.text: Restriction along an etale map is restriction to the localized etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus geometric stalks on $U$ are the same stalks as on $X$ at points of $U$, and coherence of $F|_U$ follows from its chartwise definition. Since $\operatorname{Supp}(F)=T_1\cup T_2$, its restriction has support contained in $T_2\cap|U|$. By [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], this is exactly the point set of $Z_U=Z\times_XU$. The ideal of $Z_U$ is $I|_U$ by [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence]. Apply the annihilation implication of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-ideal-power] on the Noetherian space $U$ to obtain $n\geq0$ with $(I|_U)^n(F|_U)=0$. Locally generated products commute with this restriction: both sides are generated locally by the identical products of $n$ ideal sections and one module section. Consequently $A_n|_U=0$, so every geometric stalk of $A_n$ outside $T_1$ is zero. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(A_n)\subseteq T_1$.

source.place: Tag 07UP, application of Tag 07UK on the complement of Zprime

proof.text: On the open subspace $W=X\setminus T_2$ (again [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]), $Z\times_XW$ is empty by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. The ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] identifies $I|_W$ with $\ker(\mathcal O_W\to0)=\mathcal O_W$. Therefore $A_n|_W=F|_W$: multiplication by the unit ideal generates the entire module, also for $n=0$. The quotient $B_n|_W$ is zero. Indeed cokernels are sheafified sectionwise quotients [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and restriction to this localized site computes the same local quotients. Thus all geometric stalks of $B_n$ outside $T_2$ vanish and $\operatorname{Supp}(B_n)\subseteq T_2$. This treats points outside $T_1\cup T_2$ as well as points in $T_1\setminus T_2$.

source.place: Tag 07UP, geometric-stalk calculation for Gn; the same unit-ideal calculation on the entire complement of Z

proof.text: Set $A=A_n$ and $B=B_n$ for the exponent chosen in step 3. By definition $A$ is a submodule of $F$ and $B$ its quotient, so in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] the sequence $0\to A\to F\to B\to0$ is exact: the inclusion is injective, the quotient map is locally surjective, and its kernel is precisely $A$. Step 1 gives coherence, while steps 3 and 4 give the two required support inclusions.

The item uses Z'=T_1 and Z=T_2: the submodule A has support in T_1 and the quotient B has support in T_2. The statement is unchanged and is correct, with no hypothesis added or dropped; I tested F=0, T_1 or T_2 empty, equal supports, disjoint supports and nonreduced X. The citer lem-sfb-space-coherent-ideal-filtration uses it in exactly this form. This is a plain split with no new nodes and no re-split repair note. Step 1: reduced-closed-support gives Z with |Z|=T_2; the ideal correspondence gives the quasi-coherent ideal I; the ideal-power node, under its exact hypotheses, gives coherence of I^nF and F/I^nF for every n>=0. Step 2: U=X minus T_1 is Noetherian. Quasi-compactness comes from the minimal-closed-set argument on the Noetherian |X|, which I checked. Local Noetherianity is chartwise. Quasi-separatedness comes from the qcqs-permanence clause on quasi-compact opens; it holds under either diagonal convention, because Delta_U is a base change of Delta_X along a monomorphism. Step 3: the base-change clauses of reduced-closed-support and of the correspondence identify Z_U and its ideal as I restricted to U, and 07UK on the Noetherian U gives A_n restricted to U = 0. Step 4: on W = X minus T_2, Z x_X W is empty, so I restricted to W is the unit ideal and B_n restricted to W = 0. This is elementary from the cited statements. Step 5: exactness in the abelian category of module sheaves. No statement is taken from the proof of a cited node. Duplicates: only the scheme versions exist (lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-union-exact-sequence, lem-pc-s3-coherent-reducible-support-exact-sequence); there is no space-level duplicate. I accept the tool use of lem-a1-space-etale-open-image as the generic correspondence between open subspaces and open subsets.
